{"decision":"GRANDFATHER IT. `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause` binds only on repairs recorded AFTER the cutoff. Every defect_fix / test_failure_fix recorded before it is out of the detector's scope permanently, is PARKED rather than acknowledged, and is NOT backfilled.

CUTOFF: 2026-09-06, the day `fix_without_recorded_cause` shipped (commit c681bb0, v0.50.0 item 2) — the first moment anything asked the question. Recorded at epoch:2026-09-09-the-cause-discipline-binds-forward, which is the point on the time axis; this node is the ruling made at it.

Anthony, 2026-09-09, answering the fork the requirement had carried open since 2026-08-17 and had explicitly reserved to him: "whether it is retro-fittable to the 472 events already recorded or, like dec:the-authority-check-guards-forward-not-backward, binds only forward … that is his call to make explicitly rather than mine to infer."

THE MEASUREMENT THAT MADE THIS A QUESTION, taken before it was asked rather than after (2026-09-09, against the export at docs/design/reflow2.json, which was byte-identical to the live graph):

  ChangeEvents of change_type defect_fix or test_failure_fix        259
  joined to a cause (CAUSES either way, or outgoing INVALIDATES)     31
  joined to NO cause                                                228   (88%)
  of those 228, recorded ON OR AFTER the 2026-09-06 cutoff             0

⭐ THE LAST LINE IS THE ONE THAT DECIDES IT, and it is a stronger warrant than the sibling decision had. Not one of the 228 postdates the detector. Every fix recorded since the discipline existed carries its cause — 100% forward compliance, dated 09-06, 09-06, 09-07 and onward. So the detector is not failing to be obeyed; it is reporting a backlog that accumulated while nothing asked. An unscoped check would go red on history rather than on violations, which is the exact trap dec:the-authority-check-guards-forward-not-backward names one rule over, where the comparable figure was 121 of 214 (57%) with no forward evidence available at all on day one.

WHY PARKED AND NOT ACKNOWLEDGED, because the detector offers both and they say different things. Acknowledging `fix_without_recorded_cause` says THIS DESIGN DOES NOT RECORD CAUSES and stops the question being asked ever again, including of fixes made tomorrow. That is false here and would discard a discipline currently at 100%. Parking says these 228 SPECIFIC events are out of scope and leaves the detector live for everything after them — `is_parked` skips them and the evidence line reports the parked count, so the backlog stays visible as a number rather than vanishing.

WHAT WAS REJECTED AND WHY, recorded so neither is re-litigated:

(1) RECONSTRUCT THE 228 CAUSES from the diffs. Rejected on the requirement's own argument, which is the reason the field exists at all: "the repair is recoverable from the diff; the cause is not." The events run 2026-07-23 to 2026-09-05; reconstructing a cause weeks later means inferring it, and inferred CAUSES edges are queryable and unfounded — the worst combination, and the precise ground on which the sibling decision refused to backfill 121 approver edges. It would also make the detector green BY CONSTRUCTION, which is the green-washing cap:governance-proposal's own description forbids.

(2) RECONSTRUCT ONLY THE RECENT EDGE — the 8 fixes dated 2026-09-01 to 09-05, where a session might still identify the finding each closed. Offered and not taken. It draws an arbitrary line inside the same pre-cutoff population, and the days involved are exactly the ones whose sessions have already ended; "probably still identifiable" is a hope, not evidence.

⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, stated so a later reader does not over-read it.

It does not close `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause`. The requirement's clause (c) — the design can answer what still rests on a patch — is served by `repair_report`, and that instrument reads a DIFFERENT field: the `repair` disposition on record_change (corrected_cause / contained_symptom), shipped 2026-09-09 in d2a0275. On the day this decision was written that report said UNSTATED for all 259, which is day-one and not neglect. THE SAME BOUNDARY GOVERNS IT: the disposition binds forward from its own landing and the 259 are not backfilled, for the identical reason. It raises no gap, so nothing forces the question — this paragraph exists so it is not re-opened later as though it were an oversight.

It does not touch `rule:an-issue-is-root-caused-then-pinned-by-a-test-then-fixed`, which stays advisory (enforced: false) on Anthony's 2026-08-26 word, and whose load-bearing step ② — a test observed failing BEFORE the fix — remains uncheckable from any diff or CI run.","kind":"choice","name":"The cause-recording discipline binds on fixes made from the detector's landing, not on the 228 that predate it","rationale":"228 of 259 recorded fixes carry no cause, and ZERO of them postdate the detector that asks for one — every fix recorded since 2026-09-06 is joined. The detector is therefore reporting a backlog that accumulated while nothing asked, not a discipline being ignored, and an unscoped check would go red on history rather than on violations. Reconstructing the causes would mean inferring them from diffs weeks later, producing edges that are queryable and unfounded and making the check green by construction — the ground on which the sibling authority decision refused to backfill. Parking rather than acknowledging keeps the detector live for every fix made from here, and keeps the backlog visible as a reported count instead of erasing the question.","status":"accepted"}
